title: Clinical evaluation of 3D-printed LuxaPrint Ortho Comfort occlusal splints in patients with bruxism and temporomandibular disorders: a retrospective observational study
summary:
Background: Many people grind or clench their teeth at night or during the day. Others have problems with the jaw joint and chewing muscles, such as pain or tension. These conditions are often treated with a bite splint: a custom-fitted plastic splint worn over the teeth. It protects the teeth from wear and relieves strain on the jaw and muscles. Today, such splints can be made with a three-dimensional printer.

Research question: We want to find out how durable printed bite splints made from the material LuxaPrint Ortho Comfort are in everyday dental practice. We look at how many splints are still undamaged and usable after one year, how often they needed to be adjusted, whether any unwanted effects occurred, and how satisfied patients are with their splint.

Methods: The treatment has already taken place, independently of this study. We analyse information from the treatment records of adults who received such a splint at a dental practice in Hannover between June and September 2025, focusing on the check-up appointments after about three and twelve months. In addition, participants fill in a short questionnaire once about their satisfaction with the splint. No additional examinations or treatments take place. Only data from people who have given written consent will be used.

interventions.name: Observational group (single arm, no control group): Adult patients (≥ 18 years at insertion) with sleep and/or awake bruxism and/or temporomandibular disorder (TMD) documented in the patient record who, as part of routine care received a 3D-printed occlusal splint made from LuxaPrint Ortho Comfort (

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Confirmed diagnosis of bruxism (sleep or awake) and/or temporomandibular disorder (TMD), documented in the patient record
- Treatment with a 3D-printed occlusal splint made from LuxaPrint Ortho Comfort (DMG)
- Insertion of the splint between 01 June 2025 and 30 September 2025
- Sufficient documentation in the patient record to assess the primary and secondary endpoints (at least date of insertion and clinical check-ups after approx. 3 and 12 months, or relevant information in case of premature discontinuation before 12 months)
- Age ≥ 18 years at the time of insertion
- Written informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Simultaneous use of another occlusal splint made from a different material during the same treatment period while an intact LuxaPrint Ortho Comfort splint was available (risk of confounding)
